saints.name: St. Bernard of Clairvaux
saints.title: Abbot and Doctor of the Church
saints.shortBlurb: The great Cistercian abbot and preacher whose eloquence and sanctity swayed the whole of Christendom…
biography: Born in 1090 at Fontaine-lès-Dijon of Burgundian nobility, Bernard in 1113 led some thirty companions, his brothers among them, into the reformed monastery of Cîteaux. Two years later he was sent as abbot to found Clairvaux, which under his rule sent out more than sixty daughter houses, and at Troyes in 1128 he shaped the Rule of the new Knights Templar.

The cloister could not hold him. When a double election split the papacy in 1130, Bernard judged for Innocent II and wore down the backers of Anacletus until the schism died with its claimant in 1138; in 1141 he worsted Abelard at the Council of Sens; and in 1146, at Vézelay before King Louis VII, he preached the Second Crusade at the bidding of Eugene III, once his own monk.

His eighty-six Sermons on the Song of Songs and treatises such as On Loving God and On Consideration won him the name of Mellifluous, honey-flowing, Doctor, and so he is counted patron of beekeepers. He died at Clairvaux on 20 August 1153, was canonized by Alexander III in 1174, and was declared a Doctor of the Church in 1830.
saints.knownFor: His preaching, mystical writing, and leadership of the Cistercians.

canonization.canonized: 1174 by Pope Alexander III; Doctor of the Church (1830)
